summary: This note is a short encyclopedic entry on Hagar, a biblical figure in the Book of Genesis. It describes her as an Egyptian handmaid of Sarai (Sarah) who was given to Abraham to bear a child. Her son with Abraham, Ishmael, is described as the progenitor of the Ishmaelites, and some commentators have linked her to the Hagrites.
one_line: Hagar is the Egyptian handmaid in the Book of Genesis who bore Abraham's firstborn son Ishmael.
key_facts: Hagar is a biblical person in the Book of Genesis.
Hagar was an Egyptian handmaid of Sarai (Sarah).
Sarai (Sarah) gave Hagar to Abraham to bear a child.
The product of Hagar's union with Abraham was Abraham's firstborn, Ishmael.
Ishmael is described as the progenitor of the Ishmaelites.
Various commentators have connected Hagar to the Hagrites.
Some commentators suggest Hagar may have been the eponymous ancestor of the Hagrites.
The name Hagar is given in Hebrew as הָגָר, in Tiberian as Hāgār, and in Arabic as هاجر (Hājar).
The Latin form of the name is Agar.
The note gives the English pronunciation as hay-GAR, written /heɪˈɡɑːr/.
The note states the Hebrew name's origin is of uncertain origin.
